title: Strict Mode and Common Compiler Errors
summary: TypeScript settings choose which checks the type checker makes. Strict settings help it catch more mix-ups.
introduction: TypeScript settings choose which checks the type checker makes. Strict settings help it catch more mix-ups. Think of checking every item before a class trip. Learn why missing values and unknown values need extra care.
learningObjectives: List the checks that strict enables and the optional ones tsc --init adds
Recognise TS7006, TS18048, TS2322, TS2345, TS2339 and TS2375 and explain their cause
Fix type errors honestly and migrate an existing project to strict mode step by step

blocks.text: `"strict": true` is a shortcut for a family of flags. You can set any of them individually, which is how gradual migrations work, but new projects should start with all of them. TypeScript 6 turns `strict` on by default for projects that do not set it; in 5.9 you still have to write it.

blocks.caption: Flags enabled by strict
rows: Parameters and variables whose type would silently become `any` (TS7006, TS7034)
Using a value that may be `null` or `undefined` without a check (TS18047, TS18048, TS2322)
Class fields that are not assigned in the constructor (TS2564)
Passing a callback whose parameter types are narrower than the expected signature
`this` used where its type cannot be determined
Emits `"use strict"` and parses files in JavaScript strict mode

blocks.text: The two errors you will see most

An implicit `any` and a possibly-undefined value account for most of a beginner's error list. Both appear in this short file: a parameter without a type, and the result of `Array.prototype.find`, which returns `undefined` when nothing matches.

blocks.title: implicit.ts
npx tsc implicit.ts
blocks.content:
implicit.ts:1:21 - error TS7006: Parameter 'input' implicitly has an 'any' type.

1 function parsePrice(input) {
                      ~~~~~

implicit.ts:6:13 - error TS18048: 'found' is possibly 'undefined'.

6 console.log(found.toFixed(1));
              ~~~~~


Found 2 errors in the same file, starting at: implicit.ts:1

blocks.text: The second error is not theoretical: nothing in the array is greater than 5, so running the file crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')`. The honest fixes are a real parameter type and a check for the missing case.

blocks.title: implicit-fixed.ts

blocks.text: Several checks are deliberately left out of `strict` because they change how common code is written. The 5.9 `tsc --init` template enables two of them, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and lists the style checks as comments. This file is clean under plain `strict` and fails with both extra options on.

blocks.title: exact.ts
npx tsc --exactOptionalPropertyTypes --noUncheckedIndexedAccess exact.ts
blocks.content:
exact.ts:5:7 - error TS2375: Type '{ theme: undefined; }' is not assignable to type 'Settings' with 'exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true'. Consider adding 'undefined' to the types of the target's properties.
  Types of property 'theme' are incompatible.
    Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'.

5 const settings: Settings = { theme: undefined };
        ~~~~~~~~

exact.ts:9:13 - error TS18048: 'item' is possibly 'undefined'.

9 console.log(item.toUpperCase(), settings);
              ~~~~


Found 2 errors in the same file, starting at: exact.ts:5

blocks.caption: Optional checks worth knowing
rows: `theme?: string` means *absent or a string*, not *explicitly undefined*
Methods that replace a base-class method must say `override`
Every code path of a function with a return type must return
A non-empty `case` must end with `break` or `return`
On in CI; some teams prefer a linter rule

blocks.caption: Error codes you will meet every week
rows: Type 'X' is not assignable to type 'Y'
Assigning or returning the wrong type
Argument of type 'X' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Y'
Calling a function with the wrong argument
Property 'p' does not exist on type 'T'
Typo, or a union member that lacks the property
Expected N arguments, but got M
Property missing / Object literal may only specify known properties
An object literal does not match the interface
Wrong path, missing file or missing types
Class field not assigned in the constructor

blocks.text: Three edits make any error vanish: a `// @ts-ignore` comment above the line, a `!` after the value, or an `as` cast to the type you wish you had. This file uses all three on the same bug, compiles without a single complaint, and crashes on the first call.

blocks.title: shortcuts.ts
npx tsx shortcuts.ts (tsc reports no errors)
blocks.content: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase')

blocks.title: Common mistake: treating the error as the problem
blocks.text: The error was the compiler telling you that `nickname` may be missing. `@ts-ignore`, `!`, `as` and `any` all delete the message and keep the bug. The honest fix handles the missing case: `profile.nickname?.toUpperCase() ?? "anonymous"`. If you must suppress an error, use `// @ts-expect-error` with a comment explaining why; unlike `@ts-ignore` it becomes an error itself (TS2578) once the underlying problem is fixed, so stale suppressions cannot accumulate.

blocks.title: shortcuts-fixed.ts

blocks.text: Adopting strict in an existing project

items: Enable `noImplicitAny` first and annotate parameters file by file; this is the flag with the most errors but the most mechanical fixes.
Enable `strictNullChecks` next. Expect many `possibly 'undefined'` errors; fix them with real checks, not `!`.
Switch to `"strict": true`; the remaining flags usually produce few errors.
Add `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` once the code base is stable, and run `tsc --noEmit` in CI so the error count can only go down.

blocks.title: Search by code
blocks.text: When a message is unclear, search for the code (`TS2322`) together with the type names it mentions. The code is stable across versions even when the wording changes, and the [TypeScript handbook](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/) and `tsc --explainFiles` or `--listFiles` help with module and configuration errors.

questions.question: Which option is NOT enabled by `"strict": true`?
questions.explanation: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is a separate, optional check (enabled by the 5.9 tsc --init template). The other three are part of the strict family.

questions.question: `// @ts-expect-error` reports an error if the next line no longer contains a type error.
questions.explanation: That is its advantage over @ts-ignore: an unused @ts-expect-error directive is itself reported (TS2578), so suppressions are cleaned up when the code is fixed.

seo.title: TypeScript Strict Mode – Flags and Common Compiler Errors
seo.description: What strict enables in TypeScript, the optional checks worth adding, the most common tsc error codes, and how to fix them without any, ! or @ts-ignore.
